questions.scenario: Two angry relatives are having a massive argument at an Indian wedding over some old family drama. What do you do?

options.text: Physically step in, separate them, and escort one of them to the food counter to cool off.
Listen closely to both sides to figure out the exact historical timeline of who actually started the fight years ago.
Distract everyone by loudly announcing the DJ has started playing their favorite song and dragging them to dance.
Sit them both down, calmly negotiate a compromise, and remind them that fighting will ruin the family's reputation.

questions.scenario: Your NRI cousin visits India for the very first time. How do you take charge of their trip?

options.text: Manage all the practical stuff: booking train tickets, getting them a local SIM card, and handling currency exchange.
Read up on the history of the monuments you'll visit so you can explain the exact dates and architectural facts to them.
Take them for street food, make them wear proper traditional ethnic clothes, and explain the meaning behind Indian festivals.
Act as the official spokesperson for the family, answering their tough questions about Indian politics and the economy.

questions.scenario: Your school is participating in a fierce Inter-School Debate competition. What is your role?

options.text: Running the logistics: making sure the team has their ID cards, script printouts, and water bottles ready before they go on stage.
Deeply researching the opponent's past speeches to find logical flaws, data loopholes, and weak points in their arguments.
Delivering the speech with dramatic flair, using perfect Hindi or English vocabulary and an emotional quote to win the crowd.
Taking the final closing statement, summarizing your team's stance, and masterfully destroying the opponent's main point.

questions.scenario: Your class needs a deadline extension for a huge project from the strictest teacher in school. How is it handled?

options.text: You physically collect all the half-finished notebooks and stand outside the staffroom to ensure they are received safely.
You point out a technicality in the school diary that says projects can be submitted next week without losing marks.
You make your project file look so incredibly beautiful and creative that the teacher is impressed and forgives the delay.
You confidently walk up to the teacher, explain the class's situation politely, and negotiate a solid 2-day extension for everyone.

questions.scenario: There is a massive dispute in your housing society over parking spaces. How do you respond?

options.text: Go down to the parking lot and personally help direct the cars to make sure no one is blocking the driveway.
Read the official society rulebook to see exactly what the builder legally promised about visitor parking.
Suggest organizing a society potluck dinner to calm everyone's anger and build better neighborhood relations.
Call a quick society meeting, listen patiently to both car owners, and propose a new parking schedule that works for both.

questions.scenario: You are organizing the Farewell Party for the 12th standard seniors. What is your primary focus?

options.text: Managing the entry gate, coordinating with the food caterers, and ensuring nobody creates a ruckus during the event.
Calculating the exact budget collected from the juniors and making sure the total expenses don't cross the limit.
Choreographing the main dance performance, setting up the photo booth, and selecting the perfect Bollywood retro playlist.
Hosting the event on stage, giving the main farewell speech, and making the seniors feel honored and respected.

questions.scenario: Your friend group is divided: half want to watch a Bollywood Rom-Com, and half want a South Indian Action Blockbuster.

options.text: You just take charge, book the tickets for whatever is closest, and arrange the auto-rickshaws to get everyone there on time.
You read the online reviews, check the running time, and look at box-office numbers to argue which movie is logically better.
You passionately explain the amazing music, cinematography, and cultural vibe of your choice to win them over.
You propose a deal: 'We watch the Action movie today, but the Rom-Com fans get to pick where we eat afterwards.'

questions.scenario: You are playing a highly competitive board game like Ludo, Carrom, or Monopoly with cousins.

options.text: You are the one actively setting up the board, distributing the pieces, and keeping track of whose turn it is.
You memorize the exact rules of the game and find a clever technical loophole to save your tokens from getting cut.
You keep the energy high, dramatically teasing your opponents, and making the game feel like an epic movie scene.
You secretly form a temporary alliance with another cousin to take down the strongest player on the board.

questions.scenario: There is a massive 4-hour delay at the railway station for your family's train. How do you handle it?

options.text: You stand in the inquiry line, talk to the TT, and find out exactly which platform the train is eventually arriving at.
You continuously refresh the IRCTC app to track the train's live location and calculate the exact expected delay.
You buy some local station snacks, start a loud game of Antakshari, and make the waiting time fun for the family.
You manage your parents' frustration, keep everyone calm, and weigh the pros and cons of waiting vs. booking a taxi.

questions.scenario: Your school is partnering with another school for a mega-event. What is your role?

options.text: You are responsible for managing the visiting students' transport and ensuring they all get their correct ID badges.
You carefully review the event schedule to ensure your school is getting an equal amount of stage time as the guest school.
You design the welcome ceremony, prepare the traditional Aarti/Tilak thali, and showcase your school's best talents.
You sit at the table with the Principals and Student Councils of both schools to negotiate the final joint decisions.

Embassy_Officer.title: The Ground Commander (Embassy / Consular Officer)
Embassy_Officer.primary_match_text: You are an action-oriented problem solver! You don't just talk about diplomacy; you execute it on the ground. You are reliable, organized, and great at managing people in crisis.
Embassy_Officer.day_in_the_life: Managing visa applications at foreign embassies, organizing grand Independence Day events abroad, and rescuing Indian citizens during international crises like wars or natural disasters.
Embassy_Officer.alternative_match_text: Your strong logistical and crisis-management skills would also make you an excellent Event Manager, Disaster Management Officer, or Operations Head.
Embassy_Officer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any Stream (Humanities preferred). Degree: BA in Political Science or any graduation. Next Steps: Crack the SSC CGL exam to become an Assistant Section Officer in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), or clear the UPSC Civil Services.

Treaty_Analyst.title: The Policy Decoder (Foreign Treaty / Policy Analyst)
Treaty_Analyst.primary_match_text: You have a razor-sharp, analytical mind. You love digging into the details, reading the fine print, and finding logical loopholes. You understand that international relations are built on solid laws.
Treaty_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Reading 500-page international trade agreements, analyzing data on foreign policy, and advising the government on the legal loopholes of signing a climate or defense treaty.
Treaty_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your love for research, logic, and rulebooks makes you a perfect fit for a Corporate Lawyer, Policy Researcher, or Intelligence Analyst.
Treaty_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities or Commerce. Degree: BA in Political Science, Economics, or a 5-year LLB (Law). Next Steps: Pursue a Master's in International Relations (from institutes like JNU) or International Law.

Cultural_Ambassador.title: The Global Storyteller (Cultural Ambassador / Attaché)
Cultural_Ambassador.primary_match_text: You are a creative soul who is deeply proud of your roots. You believe that food, art, cinema, and music are far more powerful in building friendships than just signing political papers.
Cultural_Ambassador.day_in_the_life: Organizing massive Yoga Day events in New York, hosting Indian food festivals in Tokyo, and promoting Bollywood cinema globally to build India's 'soft power'.
Cultural_Ambassador.alternative_match_text: If not in diplomacy, your creative storytelling and cultural pride would make you an amazing Travel Journalist, Public Relations (PR) Manager, or Arts Curator.
Cultural_Ambassador.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities / Arts. Degree: BA in History, Sociology, English, or Mass Communication. Next Steps: Master a foreign language (French, Spanish, Japanese) and apply for roles in the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).

IFS_Diplomat.title: The Master Negotiator (IFS Diplomat / UN Representative)
IFS_Diplomat.primary_match_text: You are a natural-born leader, peacemaker, and negotiator. You know how to command a room, handle pressure, and convince people to see your point of view without starting a fight.
IFS_Diplomat.day_in_the_life: Sitting at the high tables of the United Nations, wearing sharp formal clothes, debating with foreign ministers, and negotiating multi-billion dollar trade deals for India.
IFS_Diplomat.alternative_match_text: Your supreme leadership and negotiation skills would make you a brilliant Corporate CEO, Top-Tier Lawyer, or National Politician.
IFS_Diplomat.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities (History/Political Science/Economics). Degree: BA in Political Science, International Relations, or Economics. Next Steps: The ultimate goal is to crack the highly competitive UPSC Civil Services Exam and choose the Indian Foreign Service (IFS).
